title_kr: 무아론과 환원주의의 실천적 의의 고찰
title_en: A Study on the Practical Significance of Anattā and Reductionism
abstract_kr: 오늘날 인공지능과 네트워크로 대변되는 초연결사회는 인간의 활동 영역을 급격히 확장시키고 있다. 이런 변화 속에서 고정된 실체로서의 자아를 전제하는 입장은 재고될 필요가 있다. 이에 이 연구는 변화하는 환경에 부합하는 도덕적 행위자의 특성을 무아론 그리고 데릭 파핏의 환원주의를 중심으로 고찰한다. 두 이론은 모두 불변하는 실체를 부정한다는 공통점을 지닌다. 그러나 자아의 부재가 곧 윤리적 책임의 소멸을 의미하는 것은 아니다. 행위자는 고정된 실체가 아닌, 연기 혹은 심리적 연속성을 통해 어떤 연속체로서 더욱 확장된 윤리적 주체가 된다. 이 논문에서는 그와 같은 논의를 대중문화 속 캐릭터를 통해 구체화한다. 만화 ≪몬스터≫의 '요한'은 고정된 실체가 없는 존재의 유동성을 보여준다. 드라마 <샌드맨>의 '드림'은 개체가 바뀌어도 인과적 연속성을 통해 정체성이 계승됨을 시사한다. 드라마 <자백의 대가> 속 '안윤수'와 '모은'은 타인 간의 강력한 심리적 연결이 어떻게 책임을 공유하게 만드는지 예증한다. 이들은 무아와 환원주의적 자아가 현실에서 어떻게 발현될 수 있는지 보여주는 유용한 사례이다. 책임의 확장은 통시성(diachronicity)을 중심으로 검토한다. 무아론과 환원주의에서 책임은 현재에 머물지 않고 시간의 흐름을 따라 확장된다. 불교의 업(Karma)은 행위와 결과의 필연적 연속성을 강조한다. 파핏의 관계 R(Relation R) 역시 미래의 자아와 타인에게까지 책임의 범위를 넓히는 근거가 된다. 이 연구는 고정된 자아에 매이지 않을 때 책임의 범위가 확장됨을 규명한다는 데 의의가 있다. 이는 자기본위적 선택을 넘어선 보편적이고 일반화된 윤리적 판단의 가능성을 열어준다. 결론적으로 무아론과 환원주의는 현대 사회의 복잡성을 감당할 수 있는 실천적이고 유연한 윤리적 토대를 제공한다.
abstract_en: Today's hyper-connected society, characterized by artificial intelligence and networks, is rapidly expanding the scope of human activity. In these changes, the position that assumes the self as a fixed entity needs to be reconsidered. Accordingly, this study examines the characteristics of moral agents that adapt to changing environments, focusing on anattā and Derek Parfit's reductionism. To this end, I compare and analyze Buddhist anattā and Derek Parfit's reductionism. Both theories have in common that they deny the existence of unchanged entities. However, the absence of self does not necessarily mean the disappearance of ethical responsibility. The agent is not a fixed entity, but rather becomes a more expanded ethical subject as a continuum through dependent origination or psychological continuity. This paper concretizes such a discussion through characters in popular culture. ‘Yohan(Johan)’ from the cartoon ≪Monster≫ shows the fluidity of an existence without a fixed entity. ‘Dream’ in the drama < Sandman > suggests that identity is inherited through causal continuity even when an entity changes. In the drama < The Price of Confession > ‘Ahn Yoon-soo' and ‘Moeun' show how a strong psychological connection between people can lead to shared responsibility. They are useful examples of how anattā and reductionist self can manifest in reality. The expansion of responsibility is examined with a focus on diachronicity. In anattā and reductionism, responsibility does not remain in the present but extends over the time. Buddhist karma emphasizes the inevitable continuity between action and result. Parfit's Relation R also serves as a basis for expanding the scope of responsibility to the future self and others. The significance of this study lies in its demonstration that the scope of responsibility expands when one is not bound by an unchanged self. This opens up the possibility of universal and generalized ethical judgments that go beyond self-centered choices. In conclusion, anattā and reductionism provide a practical and flexible ethical foundation that can cope with the complexities of modern society.

title_kr: 세친의 ≪대승오온론≫(Pañcaskandhaka) <물질의 무더기(Rūpaskandha)> 번역 및 주해(1): 안혜의 ≪대승오온론석(Pañcaskandhakavibāṣā)≫을 참고하여
title_en: An Annotated Translation of the “Aggregate of Matter” (Rūpaskandha) from Vasubandhu’s Pañcaskandhaka (1): With Reference to Sthiramati’s Pañcaskandhakavibhāṣā
abstract_kr: 본 논문은 세친(Vasubandhu)의 ≪대승오온론≫(Pañcaskandhaka) 가운데 < 물질의 무더기(Rūpaskandha) >를 산스크리트, 한문, 티베트어를 대조하여 우리말로 번역한 것이다. 세 가지 대조를 통해 전승 과정에서 발생한 구문 상의 차이를 확인하고, 원전의 의미를 정확하게 복원하여 각 번역본의 해석적 특성을 드러내고자 한다. 아울러 안혜(Sthiramati)의 주석서인 ≪대승오온론석≫(Pañcaskandhakavibhāṣā)을 각주로 보강하여, 세친의 간결한 게송에 담긴 철학적 함의를 심화했다. 안혜는 다섯 무더기의 수와 순서, 사대종의 규정 근거, 각 요소의 고유한 특징과 상호 관계 등을 제시하면서 세친의 정의를 사상사적으로 확장하고 있다. 본 역주는 이러한 세친과 안혜의 사유를 병치하여, 유가행파 교학 체계 속에서 오온이 어떻게 재해석되는지를 조명한다.
abstract_en: This paper presents an annotated Korean translation of the “Aggregate of Matter” (Rūpaskandha) section from Vasubandhu’s Pañcaskandhaka, based on a comparative analysis of the Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan. Through this tripartite comparison, the study identifies syntactic variations that arose during textual transmission, seeks to reconstruct the original meaning with greater precision, and elucidates the interpretive characteristics of each translation. Additionally, Sthiramati’s commentary, the Pañcaskandhakavibhāṣā, is incorporated in the footnotes to deepen the philosophical implications contained in Vasubandhu’s concise verses. Sthiramati expands upon Vasubandhu’s definitions from a doctrinal-historical perspective by addressing the number and sequence of the five aggregates, the grounds for defining the four great elements (mahābhūta), and the distinctive characteristics and interrelations of each component. By juxtaposing the thought of Vasubandhu and Sthiramati, this annotated translation illuminates how the five aggregates are reinterpreted within the doctrinal framework of the Yogācāra school.

title_kr: 승무에 있어서 불교적인 것에 대하여
title_en: Regarding the Buddhist Aspects in the Korean Traditional Dance, Seungmu
abstract_kr: 본 연구의 목적은 승무를 불교사상적 관점에서 고찰함으로서 승무의 의미와 가치를 탐구하여 그 이해를 돕는데 있었다. 이를 위하여 다음과 같은 연구문제를 설정하였다. 1. 승무는 어디에서 기원하는가? 2. 승무라는 명칭은 무엇을 의미하는가? 3. 승무에 나타난 불교적 형식미는 어떤 것이 있는가? 4. 승무에 있어서 불교의 정신적 유산은 어떻게 나타나는가?이러한 제 문제를 해결하기 위하여 질적연구방법으로서 문헌고찰을 진행하였으며 후에 완전한 참여자의 입장에서 해석하였다. 첫 번째 연구 문제인 승무의 발생은 문헌을 통하여 조선중기 불교의식인 작법에서 발생하였음을 확인하였다. 두번째 연구문제인 승무라는 명칭은 스님의 복장을 한 전문예술인의 춤만을 관객의 입장에서 지칭하는 것으로 정리하였다. 세 번째 연구문제인 승무에 나타난 불교적 형식으로는 대풍류로 구성된 음악, 나비춤에서 발견되는 가사, 장삼과 고깔 그리고 법고의 세가지를 확인하였다. 네 번째 연구문제인 승무에 나타난 불교의 의식으로서 내부로 향하는 시선, 염불에서 나타나는 세 번의 오체투지 그리고 삶에 대하여 용맹정진하는 형식적 구성으로 되어 있음을 알수 있었다.그러나 공연과 학습현장에서 승무의 정신적 가치는 사라지고 무형유산으로서의 형식과 순서만이 강조되는 형해화 과정이 진행되고 있다는 것을 알 수 있었다. 무형유산 3세대로 상징되는 현 시기가 지나면 승무는 더 이상 불교의 춤으로 인식되기 힘든 지경이 될 것이다. 이를 극복하기 위하여 불교적 관점으로 승무를 이해함으로서 그 본질적 가치를 되살릴 때 올바른 승무의 전승은 가능할 것으로 기대해 본다.
abstract_en: The purpose of this study is to explore the meaning and value of Seungmu (Buddhist Ritual Dance) by examining it from the perspective of Buddhist philosophy, thereby enhancing its understanding. To achieve this, the following research questions were established: 1. What are the origins of Seungmu? 2. What does the name Seungmu signify? 3. What are the elements of Buddhist formal beauty manifested in Seungmu? 4. How is the spiritual heritage of Buddhism expressed within Seungmu?To address these questions, a qualitative research method was employed, conducting a literature review based on the research problems, followed by an interpretation from the standpoint of a complete participant. Regarding the first research question, literature confirmed that Seungmu originated from Jakbeop, a Buddhist ritual of the mid-Choseon Dynasty. For the second question, the term Seungmu was defined as referring specifically to the dance performed by professional artists dressed in monks' attire, as viewed from the audience's perspective. Thirdly, the Buddhist formal elements identified in Seungmu include music composed of Dae-pungnyu, the Gasa (monastic robe) also found in the Butterfly Dance, the Jangsam (long-sleeved robe), the Gokkal (hood), and the Beopgo (Dharma drum). Fourthly, as a manifestation of Buddhist ritual spirit, the dance incorporates an inward-looking gaze, three instances of Oche-tuji (five-point prostration) during the Buddhist invocation, and a structural progression representing Yongmaeng-jeongjin (fearless spiritual devotion).Based on these findings, it was observed that the spiritual value of Seungmu is diminishing, and a process of formalization is underway where only the external forms and sequences as intangible heritage are emphasized. As the current era, symbolized by the third generation of intangible heritage practitioners, passes, Seungmu may reach a point where it is no longer recognized as a Buddhist dance. To overcome this, this study suggests that the authentic transmission of Seungmu will be possible only when its intrinsic value is revitalized through an understanding rooted in Buddhist perspectives.

title_kr: 근대 전환기 한국불교의 사회참여와 체육운동 - 1920~30년대 불교계 축구팀의 활동
title_en: Social Participation and Sports Movement of Korean Buddhism in the Modern Transition Period - Activities of Buddhist football teams in the 1920s and 1930s
abstract_kr: 본 연구는 일제강점기 근대 전환기 한국불교의 사회참여가 체육운동, 특히 축구 활동을 매개로 어떠한 방식으로 구현되었는지를 고찰한다. 분석 대상은 1920~30년대 불교계 청년조직(조선불교청년회 등)과 불교계 축구팀의 활동이며, 종교단체의 스포츠 참여를 단순한 여가나 주변적 사건이 아니라 청년운동의 조직 실천이자 대중 접점 확장 전략으로 재해석하는 데 목적이 있다. 연구는 날짜·일정·일부 스코어 및 포지션 표기 등 목록형 경기 기록과 언론·회고 성격의 기사 자료를 결합하여, 개별 경기의 상세 서사를 복원하기 어렵다는 자료적 한계를 전제하면서도 일정의 밀집과 분포를 통해 ‘대회 시즌’이라는 사회적 시간 구조를 복원하였다. 이를 바탕으로 불교 청년조직이 시즌 시간표에 맞춰 인적·물적 자원을 동원·배치하고, 경기 참여를 통해 단체의 가시성을 확보하며 내부 결속과 규율을 강화하는 과정을 논증한다. 또한 팀 운영의 지속 가능성 관점에서 재정·시설·인력 유지의 제약이 조직의 재편 및 정체성 조정으로 이어질 수 있음을 가설적으로 제시하고, 신문 원문 대조와 대회 등록 자료, 내부 문서의 추가 확보를 통해 해당 가설을 검증할 수 있는 연구 설계를 제안한다. 본 연구는 근대 한국불교사의 사회참여를 정치·제도 중심 서술에서 확장하여, 문화 실천과 신체 훈련이라는 차원에서 종교와 대중문화의 접합 양상을 해명한다.
abstract_en: This study aims to examine how Korean Buddhism's social participation was realized through physical culture in the process of transitioning to colonial modernity, especially soccer. The analysis focuses on the activities of Buddhist youth groups (including the Chosun Buddhist Youth Association) and Buddhist soccer teams in the 1920s and 1930s, and aims to reinterpret religious groups' participation in sports as a strategy to expand contact with the wider public, not just leisure or surrounding episodes.Methodologically, the study combines a catalogued match record consisting mainly of date, schedule, and partial score/position notation with press materials containing retrospective or interpretive elements. While acknowledging the archival limitations that such data do not allow for a complete reconstruction of detailed match narratives, the study reconstructs the social time structure of the 'contest season' by analyzing the clustering and distribution of recorded match schedules. On this basis, Buddhist youth organizations claim to have mobilized and allocated human and material resources according to the seasonal timetable, secured public visibility through participation in matches, and strengthened internal cohesion and discipline.From the perspective of organizational sustainability, this study proposes a working hypothesis that restrictions on finance, facilities, and manpower maintenance can lead to organizational restructuring and identity adjustment. To test this hypothesis, we outline a research design that requires triangulation of newspaper original texts, contest registration data, and additional internal documents. By expanding research on participation in Korean Buddhist society beyond a political-institutional narrative, this article aims to clarify the interface between religion and popular culture through cultural practice and physical training in the modern era.

title_kr: 인도에서 동아시아로 전파된 한국의 명왕신앙 고찰
title_en: A Study on Korean Vidyārāja (Myeongwang) Worship: Its Transmission from India to East Asia
abstract_kr: This paper examines the historical aspects of Myeongwang(Vidyārāja) worship in Korean Buddhism, particularly focusing on Fudo Myoo(Acala). While Myeongwang is commonly understood in Korea as an influence of Japanese Buddhism, evidence of Myeongwang worship can actually be found in existing Korean artifacts and ritual texts. Specifically, among the Myeongwang, Fudo Myoo is viewed as an influence of Japanese Shingon Buddhism during the Japanese colonial period, and many people hold negative perceptions of this deity. This is due to insufficient research in this field, and the fact that the most well-known example of Myeongwang is the Fudo Myoo statue carved alongside Kukai at Mt. Yudalsan in Mokpo, which is considered a product of Japanese Buddhist worship during the colonial period. This paper demonstrates that as Myeongwang spread from India to East Asia, it developed differently in each region, and in Korea, other Myeongwang, especially Ucchuṣma, were much more popular than Fudo Myoo. Furthermore, this study aims to understand that Myeongwang worship existed throughout the history of Korean Buddhism, not just during the Japanese colonial period, and examines how Fudo Myoo was manifested within this context.

title_kr: 초연결사회(hyper-connected society)와 불성의 확장 가능성 모색
title_en: Hyper-connected Society and Exploring the Possibilityof Expanding of Buddhahood
abstract_kr: The Fourth Industrial Revolution is accelerating the transition towards a hyper-connected society centered around ICBM (Internet of Things, Cloud Computing, Big Data, and Mobile). In this hyper-connected society, the boundaries between subjects and objects become blurred. However, this does not necessarily mean a desirable harmony. In this situation, the essential thing is the soundness of the hyper-connected society's network and its users. Buddhahood is the fundamental nature in all beings. Because of this buddhahood, beings can transform while maintaining their identity, and this transformation can lead to good. This buddhahood can be expanded through the recognition of dependent origination and the practice of compassionate action. This has significant implications for the hyper-connected society. Even in a state of accelerated interconnection between humans and objects, humans remain crucial. The quality and quantity of the cloud and big data, which directly influence the state of the hyper-connected society, are determined by individual users and the relationships they form. Reflection on buddhahood can provide valuable guidance on what humans should do and what kind of beings they should be in a hyper-connected society. This can positively contribute to the connection between humans, networks, and the Internet of Things.

title_kr: 1920년대 불교계 소년야구단 설립과 활동 연구 -대구불교청년회 소년야구단을 중심으로 -
title_en: A Study on the Establishment and Activities of Buddhist-Affiliated Juvenile Baseball Teams in the 1920s - Focusing on the Daegu Buddhist Youth Association’s Juvenile Baseball Team
abstract_kr: This study examines the establishment and activities of the Buddhist Youth Association’s juvenile baseball team in Daegu during the 1920s, highlighting the historical significance of Buddhist-affiliated sports activities under Japanese colonial rule. Modern baseball was introduced to Korea in 1896 and became systematically organized in the 1920s. During this period, religious organizations, including Buddhist groups, actively formed youth baseball teams as part of their educational and social efforts. Particularly after the March 1st Movement, during Japan’s so-called “Cultural Rule” period, religious organizations reinforced their youth education and social programs, with sports activities playing a key role. The Daegu Buddhist Youth Association, founded in 1920, established an athletic division and launched a juvenile baseball team to promote modern sports education.The juvenile baseball team consisted of players aged 10 to 15, who engaged in regular training, participated in local tournaments, and traveled for interregional matches. The team’s 1921 expedition to Miryang is regarded as one of the earliest cases of an official game played by a team composed entirely of players under 15. In the same year, the team won the Daegu Youth Baseball Tournament, demonstrating the Buddhist community’s success in fostering youth sports. Additionally, the celebratory car parade and community events following their victory suggest that Buddhist organizations played a significant role in regional exchanges and youth movements through sports.This study utilizes newspaper articles, Buddhist periodicals, and regional historical records to analyze the operational structure and societal impact of the baseball team. The findings indicate that Buddhist-affiliated sports activities were not merely recreational but served as an essential component of modern youth education and nationalist movements during the colonial era. Moreover, the study highlights how Buddhist organizations transcended religious boundaries to contribute to regional development and sports promotion. By broadening the scope of research on Korea’s modern sports history and the role of religious groups in youth movements, this study offers valuable insights into the contemporary role of religious organizations in youth sports education.

title_kr: 제천 경은사 목조문수보살좌상 연구
title_en: A Study on the Wooden Seated Statue of Manjushri Bodhisattva at Gyeongeunsa Temple in Jecheon
abstract_kr: The This study examines the Buddhist sculptor Seungil (勝一) and his role in creating the wooden seated statue of Manjushri Bodhisattva enshrined at Gyeongeunsa Temple (慶恩寺) in Jecheon.The statue, produced in December 1636, follows the Ilmokshik (一木式) technique and stands 30 cm in height. It is characterized by a meditative posture (Dhyana Mudra, 禪定印), a proportionally large head, a slightly forward-leaning torso, and distinct drapery patterns.The inscription reveals that Seungil sculpted the statue, while Hye-yun (惠允) crafted the pedestal. The project was supervised by Doin (斗仁) and managed by Johaeng (祖行), both of whom were involved in major Buddhist projects at Muryangsa Temple (無量寺) in Buyeo. These connections indicate that the statue was originally produced at Muryangsa before being relocated to Gyeongeunsa.Seungil, born around 1590, initially worked as an assistant sculptor in the early 17th century. By the 1620s, he was collaborating with his mentor Hyeonjin (玄眞) and later worked alongside sculptors like Muyeom (無染) and Cheongheon (淸憲). From the 1630s onward, he took on leadership roles in Buddhist sculpture projects, extending his activities across the Yeongnam and Honam regions until the 1670s. His career, spanning approximately 50 years, establishes him as a representative Buddhist sculptor of the mid-17th century.Additionally, this study explores Seungil’s role within a Buddhist sculptural tradition, tracing the transmission of artistic techniques and stylistic characteristics from his teacher Hyeonjin (玄眞) to subsequent sculptors, including Eung-hye (應惠), Heejang (熙藏), Gyechan (戒贊), and Dojam (道岑). His contributions provide significant insights into the development of Buddhist sculpture in 17th-century Korea.

title_kr: 유식사상과 실천 - <단순구조>와 입무상방편과의 관계를 중심으로 -
title_en: Doctrine and Practice in Vijñāna-vāda, With an Emphasis on the Relationship between “Simple Structures” and the “Expedient Means of Entering Formlessness”
abstract_kr: This text is a Korean translation of the Japanese paper ““Doctrine and Practice in Vijñāna-vāda, With an cEmphasis on the Relationship between “Simple Structures” and the “Expedient Means of Entering Formlessness”” by Kitano Shintaro (北野 新太郎). The author, Kitano, meticulously analyzes the relationship between the Yogācāra theory of three natures and the theory of two graspings and two divisions (二取·二分), the schema of ‘simple structure’ and ‘double structure’, and the philological and philosophical contextual differences among vijñaptimātratā (唯識實性), vijñaptimātra (唯識性), and vijñānamātratva (唯識). Overall, this paper demonstrates the various approaches and interpretive differences in early Yogācāra thought research, as well as the resulting complexities in academic discussions. The translator has converted all endnotes from the original text into footnotes for easier reading. It is hoped that this translation will be of great help not only to domestic specialists in early to middle Indian Yogācāra studies but also to scholars in other fields in understanding Yogācāra thought. The translator sincerely thanks Professor Kitano for granting permission for this translation.

title_kr: 전통 불교문화유산을 활용한 한국 웰니스(wellness)관광 발전 방안 연구
title_en: Research on Developing Korean Wellness Tourism by Utilizing Traditional Buddhist Cultural Heritage
abstract_kr: Korean Buddhism has developed unique tangible and intangible cultural heritage that promotes both mental peace and physical health, pursuing harmony and coexistence with nature. Formed over a long period, Korea’s traditional Buddhist cultural heritage aligns with modern society’s goals of environmental conservation, community coexistence, and sustainable development. It also directly connects with various domains of the wellness industry, which has garnered significant global attention in the post-pandemic era.Among the traditional Buddhist cultural heritage, intangible assets such as Seon meditation, prostrations and the 108 bows, temple food, traditional alms bowl meals, tea ceremonies, and dancheong (traditional decorative coloring on wooden structures) hold significant potential as new realms of wellness tourism aimed at healing the mind and body.Developing wellness tourism programs based on traditional mountain temples and Buddhist practices, along with efforts in international promotion, marketing, and regional specialization strategies, can not only revitalize wellness tourism utilizing Buddhist cultural heritage but also serve as a crucial opportunity to spread K-Buddhism worldwide.

title_kr: 전통문화산업을 세계불교시장과 연결하는 글로벌전략 방안에 관한 연구
title_en: Research on a global strategy to connect traditional cultural industries with the global Buddhist market
abstract_kr: 본 연구는 전통문화산업이 세계 불교 시장과 연결될 수 있는 글로벌 전략 방안을 모색하고자 한다. 이를 위해 먼저 전통문화산업의 개념과 현황을 분석하고, 불교의 종교적, 문화적 가치를 중심으로 글로벌 네트워크를 구축하고, 디지털 기술과 융합한 혁신적인 방안을 제시하며, 지역 특화 콘텐츠와 문화외교를 활용하는 방안을 제시하고자 한다.이를 바탕으로 다음과 같은 글로벌 전략 방안을 제시하였다. 서울 국제불교 박람회는 불교의 종교적 가치를 기반으로 전통문화와 현대적 콘텐츠를 융합하여 글로벌 플랫폼으로 확장할 잠재력을 지니고 있다.첫째, 전통문화산업의 콘텐츠를 불교적 요소와 결합하여 전통문화와 웰니스 서비스를 개발하는 것이다. 예를 들어, 전통적인 공예품에 불교적인 문양을 추가하거나, 불교적인 컨텐츠를 담은 이야기를 담은 공연이나 전시를 기획하는 것이다. 둘째, 세계 불교 시장의 수요를 파악하여, 이를 충족시킬 수 있는 제품이나 서비스를 제공하는 것이다. 셋째, 전통문화산업의 브랜드 이미지를 강화하여, 세계 불교 시장에서 경쟁력을 높이는 것이다.본 연구는 불교박람회가 전통문화와 현대적 트렌드를 아우르는 글로벌 문화산업으로 자리 잡는 데 기여할 수 있다.이를 통해 불교박람회는 단순한 종교행사를 넘어 전통문화와 웰니스 트렌드를 아우르는 국제적인 교류의 장으로 자리 잡을 가능성을 논의한다.서울 국제 불교박람회의 브랜딩 전략을 통해 한국의 대중 불교박람회를 전세계에 효율적으로 전파하고, 궁극적으로는 국가이미지 제고를 목표로 하여 브랜딩 전략모델 및 세부적 실행방안을 제시하고자 한다.장기적인 관점에서 한국 전통문화산업과 MICE산업을 연계하여 세계인들과 함께 문화교류를 할 수 있는 대표브랜드로 거듭날 수 있도록 해야 할 것이다.이러한 전략적 접근은 불교의 정신적 가치와 문화적 유산을 세계에 알리는 동시에, 경제적 가치와 문화교류를 증진하는 데 중추적인 역할을 할 것이다.

title_kr: ‘전통문화산업진흥법’의 제정 의미와 전망
title_en: Meaning and prospects of the enactment of the ‘Traditional Cultural Industry Promotion Act”
abstract_kr: In 2024, the Traditional Culture Industry Promotion Act was enacted, and an enforcement decree was prepared accordingly, and a basic plan for five years was also enacted and announced. The specificity of this law was examined through the process of enacting the Traditional Culture Industry Promotion Act for more than 15 years. And based on this, the direction of the law was analyzed by analyzing the scope of the subject and industrial identity of this law. Finally, the advantages and disadvantages of the basic plan made based on this law are analyzed, and based on this, the direction of development is suggested.The research results are summarized as follows.First, the Traditional Culture Industry Promotion Act clearly defines traditional culture as cultural resources, and traditional culture industry promotes promotion policies according to the industrial identity of cultural industry of creative industries with creativity as their core.Second, the traditional culture industry is basically a resource convergence industry. The industry-centered promotion policy centered on 6H (Korean house, Korean food, hanbok, Korean paper, Korean music, and Hangeul) that the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism has been promoting since the 2007 Korean Style Promotion Comprehensive Plan showed limitations. As a cultural industry, the traditional culture industry is a convergence industry with strong characteristics of the modern 4th industry that has a virtuous cycle system of the value chain at its core.Third, there is an urgent need for a long-term and regular survey of the entire scope of the Traditional Culture Industry Promotion Act (traditional lifestyle and traditional arts). Traditional cultural industries have a large number of domestic handicrafts and have great difficulty in investigating the actual conditions, such as existing as part of the modern industry. As stipulated by the law, it is necessary to develop them to become national approval statistics of the National Statistical Office beyond conducting surveys every two years.Fourth, for the efficient success of the Traditional Culture Industry Promotion Act and the Basic Plan, it is necessary to form a pan-government promotion committee. Traditional culture industry promotion laws and policies are distributed and carried out in various government ministries and agencies such as the Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs (Korean Food), the Ministry of Land, Transport and Maritime Affairs (Hanok), and the National Heritage Administration (Intangible Heritage), making it difficult to obtain the efficiency of the project. Since it may be difficult to proceed efficiently at the level of requesting cooperation within the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, a more clear pan-government promotion system under the Prime Minister should be established.Fifth, the traditional cultural industry promotion project should focus on 'popularization' as the core of the strategy that is urgent at this stage. Considering the poor situation of the traditional cultural industry, it is most important to create and expand the demand for traditional cultural products. In addition, even in these efforts to create demand, an approach for cultural industries such as storytelling products and principles that prioritize private companies are needed.The Traditional Culture Industry Promotion Act, which began to take effect in 2024, has now taken its first step. Below, efforts should be made to realize promotion policies tailored to the specificity of the industrial site, and above, wisdom should be gathered so that promotion projects tailored to the trends of the modern industry can be promoted based on the industrial identity of the cultural industry.

title_kr: 근대 화승 문고산이 재현한 북송 소식의 <십팔대아라한송>
title_en: <The Eighteen Great Arahan Song> of Su Shi(蘇軾) from the Northern Song Dynasty reproduced by Mun Go-san(文古山), one of the Modern Monk Painter.
abstract_kr: The monk painter(畵僧) Mun Go-san(文古山. c. 1850-c. 1930) was a Buddhist artist(佛母) at Yujeomsa Temple(楡岾寺) on Mt. Geumgangsan and was active in Korea and left many Buddhist paintings throughout the late Joseon Dynasty, the Korean Empire, and the Japanese colonial period and was introduced to the media as a representative Buddhist painting producer in the early 20th century. His surname in worldly life(俗性) is Mun, and his Buddhist name is Gosan Chuk-yeon(古山竺衍). He became famous as a painter at Mt. Geumgang, and it seems he had a great pride in his paintings. He left his signature on the Buddhist paintings he created and used his creativity to produce many Buddhist paintings withhis own personalityIn this study, we looked at the Sixteen Arhats(十六羅漢圖) among the Buddhist paintings produced by Mun Go-san, in which his creativity and diverse capabilities were well demonstrated. There are many paintings of Arhats from Mun Go-san, and due to the nature of Arhat paintings, they are set against landscapes, and the various appearances of Arhats and their dependents and environments appear in a variety of ways, making them a representative group of works that clearly show the characteristics of the works among his Buddhist paintings. In particular, the figures of Arhats he depicts actively express the contents of < The Eighteen Arhat Songs (十八大阿羅漢頌) > by Su Shi (蘇軾, 1037-1101), a writer of the Northern Song Dynasty, while also expressing elements that allowed him to sense his unique painting style and the spirit of the times, making them very interesting.

title_kr: 만공(滿空) 문하 견성암과 환희대의 비구니 문중에 관한 일고
title_en: A consideration about the nuns’ clans of Mangong disciples with Gyeonseongam and Hwanheedae
abstract_kr: It deals with the transmission of nuns centered around Sudeoksa Temple.I looked into the nuns’ clans that occupied half of Korean Buddhism, and especially Gyeonseongam and Hwanheedae of Sudeoksa in Deoksungchonglim. I studied the research in chronological order from nuns’ clans which were established at the time of Buddha to the nuns clan in Korea, and then the nuns clan of Gyeonseongam and Hwanheedae.The nuns’ clans of Sudeoksa are spread throughout the country, and most of them have taken root at Sudeoksa. Nuns who learned Zen under Mangong at Sudeoksa are prospered and Buddhist doctrine of nuns was formed around them. Next, I introduced Gyeonseongam and Hwanheedae among the nuns clans of Sudeoksa in Deoksungchonglim.Through this study, we understand that nuns’ clans centered around Sudeoksa have been handed down, and it was connected through Buddhist doctrine, not blood relations. However, we also learned that social customs centered on blood relations still have strong power. It is necessary to discuss in public in order to get social and cultural recognition for the transmission of Buddhism and to be recognized as customary law, and I pointed out the importance to inform the current status of transmission of teacher and pupil.

title_kr: “근대불교 강맥(講脈)의 사자상승 연구 - 석전 박한영을 중심으로”
title_en: A study Sajasangseung(師資相承) in Gangmaek(講脈) of modern Buddhism - Focusing on Seokjeon Park Han-yeong”
abstract_kr: Korean Buddhism has traditionally placed great importance on Ganhwaseon(看話禪). A similar pattern continued in modern times, but modern studies were accepted to expand teaching.In particular, Park Han-young, Jin Eung-hyechan, Geum Bong-yeon, Jin Ho Seok-yeon, Toekyung-ro, and Fogwang Young-soo took on the role of teachers. In the first half of the 20th century, they took on the role of teaching their disciples. And they passed on their Gangmaek (講脈) to those who were qualified to cultivate future generations.Park Han-young emphasized nurturing talent, saying, “Education is more important than anything else.” Park Han-young, who produced major scholars of modern and contemporary Korean Buddhism, is a representative monk who maintained the identity of Joseon Buddhism and communicated with independence activists during the Japanese colonial period.Park Han-young's disciples include Ungi Sung-won, Un Yong-ha, Unseong Seung-hee, Go Bong Tae-soo, Sung Neung Bok-mun, Cheol Un Jong-hyun, Myeongbong, and Hakbong. Park Han-young's students have been identified so far, with a total of 165.Among his disciples, he taught students at major educational institutions, including the president of Dongguk University, a professor at Chung-Ang University, the president of Haein Temple Sangha University, the president of Donghwa Temple Sangha University, the president of Donghwasa Sangha University, the president of Unmun Temple Sangha University, and the president of Bongnyeong Temple Sangha University. There are also many disciples who held important positions in the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism.The disciples of Seokjeon Park Han-yeong had a great influence on the development of modern Korean Buddhism and Buddhist studies.

title_kr: 조선후기 승려의 법맥과 특징 - 대흥사(大興寺)를 중심으로 -
title_en: A Study on Dharma lineage and characteristics of Buddhist monks in the late Joseon Dynasty - Focusing on Daeheung Temple -
abstract_kr: Seon(禪)'s tradition was passed down through Saja Sangseung(師資相承), where a teacher transmits the law to his disciples. The transmission of the law from a teacher to his disciples was considered very important in terms of respect for orthodoxy or the succession of a religious order. In Korea as well, the law of Seon in the concept of factions, which sought to assert the legitimacy of one's own faction, centered on the dharma lineage between teachers and disciples, emerged in the mid-to-late Joseon Dynasty. In particular, Daeheung Temple(大興寺) located in Jeollanam-do Haenam claimed the legitimacy of the sect through the establishment of the Cheongheo(淸虛) legal lineage.Among the Cheongheo-line(淸虛系), the Pyeonyang faction(鞭羊派) and the Soyo faction(逍遙派) expanded their influence around Daeheung Temple from the late 17th century. Cheongheo's disciple Pyeonyang Eongi(鞭羊彦機) established Cheongheo's lineage by emphasizing the lineage of the Linji School(臨濟宗) leading to Linji(臨濟), Seogok(石屋), and Taego Bou(太古普愚), and asserted the legitimacy of the Cheongheo-line.In addition, the fact that the Pyeonyang faction and the Soyo faction seek to emphasize the legitimacy of the legal lineage is also shown in ‘Cheongheo Yueui(淸虛遺意)’, in which Cheongheo had his ceremonial cape and bowl(衣鉢) delivered to Daeheung Temple. The Pyeonyang faction and Soyo faction, who were active around Daeheung Temple, took advantage of this to highlight Daeheung Temple.As Daeheung Temple was designated as Pyochung-sa(表忠祠), Daeheung Temple was officially recognized as a temple that inherited the Buddhist tradition of Cheongheo. This series of processes was expanded to present Daeheung Temple as Jongweon(宗院), and Jongweon was framed as a system of 12 representative Seon preceptors(12宗師) and 12 doctrinal preceptors(12講 師) consisting of the Pyeonyang faction and the Soyo faction.These 12 representative Seon preceptors and 12 doctrinal preceptors show two structures : inheriting the teachings of the Linji School(臨濟宗) and passing on the Huayan Study(華嚴學). Through this, Daeheung Temple produced excellent Seon masters and excellent instructors, and the prestige of Daeheung Temple was able to further expand after the 18th century.

title_kr: 僧侶門中의 형성과 법맥 전승의 상징, 高僧眞影
title_en: Monk Portraits: Symbol of Monk Lineage Formation and Dharma Transmission
abstract_kr: Monk portraits have been vaguely known as one of the signs of Dharma transmission in the relationship of master and disciple(師資相承). However, the nature of monk portraits produced in the late Joseon Dynasty is more complex, and the backgrounds, processes, and outcomes of their creation vary widely. In order to understand the diversity of late Joseon Buddhist culture reflected in the monk portraits, this article examines Yeonggak, the Buddhist hall for enshrining the monk portraits, the monk lineages of the project entities that produced the portraits and promoted the process of enshrining them in the Yeonggak, and the intention of enshrining not only portraits of direct masters but also portraits of prominent monks unrelated to the Dharma lineage, using Bongjeongsa Temple, Songgwangsa Temple, Haeinsa Temple, and Magoksa Temple as examples. This study found that the monk portraits enshrined in the temples reflected the fact that the various monk lineages which flourished in the late Joseon Dynasty acknowledged and respected the history of the monks who lived in the temples before them. It also suggested that the portraits were the result of movements, changes, and perceptions of the times, as they connected themselves with that history to establish and symbolize the orthodoxy of the community.

title_kr: 선학원의 설립 주체와 노선에 대한 재검토
title_en: Reexamination of the establishment and route of Seonhakwon
abstract_kr: This review is an article dealing with the history and characteristics of Seon Academy, which has an important status in the modern and contemporary history of Korea. However, recently, disagreements over the history, culture, identity, and route of Seon Academy have been controversial. At the bottom of the controversy are the confrontation between the Jogye Order and the Seon Academy, the heterogeneous lines, and the alteration of the history of the Seon Academy.With this premise, I have dealt with the following aspects in this review. First, it was emphasized that the main body of the establishment and operation of Seon Academy is Monk Mangong of Sudeoksa Temple. This is a criticism of the perception that the current Seon Academy executive department tries to view Manhae Han Yong-un as an ‘investigation of establishment’. Therefore, I refuted the argument of the judgment made by Beopjin of Seonhawon by reason and logic. Second, the documents submitted by Beomeosa during the trial with the Seon Academy were excavated and the contents contained therein were introduced. The content is that a female believer named Choi Chang-woon has nothing to do with Han Yong-un, and is a supporter of Baek Yong-seong. And Han Yong-un was an independence activist who had no close contact with Shinto. Third, it was emphasized that the line of Seonhakwon should not be oriented towards the end, but should be directed towards the line of precedence. Therefore, in 1967, the “practice guide” claimed by Lee Daewe, the president of Seon Academy, was excavated and introduced. Fourth, the 100-year history published by Seonhakwon, 'Memories of 100 Years of Seonhakwon', was criticized. In that book, he pointed out the contradiction of seeing Yongun Han as a founding investigation, the imbalance in the description of the main characters of the Seon Academy, and the absurd description of the history of Sudeok.I hope that this logic and argument of the author will be helpful in understanding the history and culture of Seonwon. Furthermore, I hope that the Jogye Order and Seon Academy will serve as a reference on the way from confrontation to reconciliation and normalization.

title_kr: 일제강점기 한국불교 자주화 및 정체성 구현 활동 연구 - 임제종, 선우공제회, 유교법회 등 참여 인사를 중심으로 -
title_en: Period of Japanese occupation A Study on the Activities of Korean Buddhism's Self-reliance and Identity Implementation
abstract_kr: Japanese colonial era Korean Buddhism underwent major and minor twists and turns in the special circumstances of colonization. There are many cases in which pro-Japanese forces have been nurtured and taken control of the temple.Monks with nationalistic tendencies continued to respond. They were struggling to adhere to the legitimacy of Korean Buddhism and clean practice.Activities for realizing the identity of Korean Buddhism were succeeded after liberation on August 15, 1945 through the Japanese colonial period. It led to a Buddhist purification movement to liquidate pro-Japanese forces and restore orthodoxy(宗統), and in 1962, it became the foundation for the launch of the Unified Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism.The reason for the revival of Korean Buddhism while maintaining its reputation is that there was a public who agreed and participated as much as leaders-level monks. Leaders played an important role, and many monks decorated a page of history without leaving a trace.Some showed pro-Japanese activities, but they did not account for the majority in numbers. Rather, there were many monks who actively participated in the independence movement. Korean Buddhist monks made every effort to come up with self-rescue measures in Japanese colonial era. In the meantime, some leaders have been diagnosing and analyzing the reality of Korean Buddhism during the Japanese colonial rule, but now it is necessary to shed light on the activities and participation of unnamed monks.Modern Korean Buddhism has undergone tremendous trials.In this process, it has often been criticized and supported, but it should not be forgotten that the monks want to inherit the wisdom of the Buddha and build a community that is not affected by foreign powers in the difficult situation of losing the country.

title_kr: ≪경허집≫으로 보는 한국불교의 수행문화
title_en: The Performance Culture of Korean Buddhism in Gyeongheo-jip ≪鏡虛集≫
abstract_kr: This study is a series of attempts to study Gyeongheo unbiasedly, the Joongheungjo(中興祖) of modern Zen Buddhism. Text is Gyeongheo-jip≪鏡虛集≫ and through this, the performance culture of Korean Buddhism was studied. The basic performances of Buddhism are kangyeong(看經), Zen meditation(參禪), Yeombul(念佛), and Jigye(持戒). The study examines how this was implemented in the ideology of Gyeongheo, the convergence of missionary work and Jeongto(淨土), which is a characteristic of Korean Buddhism.A specific analysis was attempted in three sentences excluding poetry.First, the Seongyo(禪敎) application and the idea of Maitreya Jeongto(彌勒淨土) were discussed in the <結同修定慧同生兜率同成佛果稧社文>.Second, in <泥牛吼>, I looked at Gyeongheo's meditation guidance and interpretation of Yukbaramil(六波羅密).Third, Yeombul(念佛) and Jigye(持戒) were examined in <與藤菴和尙>. Yeombul(念佛) is a 定心念佛, and Jigye(持戒) claims a Mahayana sila(大乘戒).Gyeongheo's sentence is characterized by an unpainted natural and cool style. Sometimes a dialogue is used to remind younger students in detail. Gyeongheo revived modern Zen Buddhism in Korea by awakening his juniors with sentences and practicing and guiding in person.

title_kr: 경허선사의 간화선에 대한 고찰
title_en: A study on the Ganhwa Seon of Gyeongheo
abstract_kr: This paper examines Gyeongheo’s Ganhwa Seon in the tradition of Ganhwa and examines the significance of Gyeongheo’s Ganhwa Seon through the characteristics of the Hwadu he emphasized and practiced. These attempts were discussed from three perspectives. First, Ganhwa Seon of Gyeongheo is greatly related to the issue of life and death, and how this point is ideologically connected with Daehui(大慧)’s Ganhwa Seon was examined. Gyung-heo realized the problem of life and death through fear of death, and started practicing Ganhwa as an alternative to overcome the problem of life and death. Gyeongheo sublimated the critical mind about life and death into doubt of Hwadu, which coincides with the study method of Hwadu suggested by Daehui. Second, I looked into Gyeongheo’s Mujahwadu. Gyeongheo suggested Mujahwadu as a method of inquiry. This mujahwadu is a representative Hwadu that symbolizes Ganhwa Seon, and it is a Hwadu that was valued by Chinese and Korean Ganhwa Seon masters such as Daehui, Jinul(知訥), Bowu(普愚), and Cheongheo(淸虛). Gyeongheo presented Mujahwadu in two ways: Danjae(單提) and Jeonje(全提). Danje and Jeonje each have functions to replace scattered mind and unstable mind, and Gyeongheo appropriately presented the method of doubting Mujahwadu according to the situation or base. Third, I looked into Gyeongheo’s ‘What is this’ Hwadu. Gyungheo is one of the Seon masters who formally presented the ‘What is this’ Hwadu, which has traditionally been handed down to Seon schools. Instead of asking abstract essences such as One-Thing, One’s original face, etc., he doubted what causes the action of seeing, hearing, speaking, and moving now and what it looks like. In addition, Gyeongheo asked Illuminating Mind(昭昭靈靈) what the subject of perception was and reflected on it, which is different from the traditional ‘What is this’ Hwadu that asks about ‘the essence of One-Thing’. Gyeong-heo inherited the tradition of the Hwadu appeared in Susimgyeol, but he changed it into Korean and presented the Hwadu in a way that further strengthened the doubt of Hwadu, which is different from Jinul.

title_kr: 불교의 철학적 토론전통 ― 불교, 그리고 서사(敍事)
title_en: A tradition of Buddhist Discourses as Philosophy: Buddhism and Narrative
abstract_kr: Philosophical inquiry starts with a debatable question, that is, a question which arises in a context in which doubt is possible. But it is more than that. A philosophical question is a question of genuine inquiry, which is one which has no pat answer that is obvious from the outset. In his discourses of the Sutta Piṭaka the Buddha engages other teachers in question and answer debates in which they themselves inquire and learn. There is an heuristic rule of non-contradiction in these debates, which is that one cannot continue in the debate if he contradicts himself three times without admitting the self-contradiction. Buddha uses several argument strategies in dealing with questions from Jains, Brahmins, and others. The discourses of the Buddha that report dialogues in real life with names and places. By reading them one sees that philosophical dialogue takes place in the stories. Buddha’s discourses are specific but are related to broader philosophical discussions of consistency and self-contradiction, fact, evidence, argument, and the achievement of wisdom. These broader concerns are neither Asian nor Western, but human concerns. The purpose of this paper is to highlight Buddha’s contribution to doing philosophy in narrative discourse.

title_kr: 본생담 문헌에 나타난 석가보살의 마지막 10개의 전생이야기 - 테라와다 불교전승
title_en: The Ten Last Lives of Bodhisatta in Jātaka Stories: Narrating in Theravāda Buddhism
abstract_kr: The aim of this article is to study and present Mahanipata Jataka Murals in Thai Temples. The final ten stories, called tot-sahchat chah-dok (ทศชาติชาดก) or phra-jao-sip-chat (พระเจ้าสิบ ชาติ) in Thai and the Mahanipata Jataka in English (often known as “The Ten Great Birth Stories of the Buddha”), are morality tales in which the Bodhisatta (what a Buddha-to-be is called) develops the ten paramitas (“perfections of character”) that one needs to master in order to reach enlightenment. Mural paintings of these ten Jataka are common features in temples in Thailand but you need to know the stories to understand these ubiquitous pictures.

title_kr: 언어와 공안(公案) 수행 - 지눌(知訥)과 메를로-퐁티(Merleau-Ponty)의 저서에 나타난 제스처 (Gesture)에 대한 연구
title_en: Language and Kong-an (公案) Practice: An Investigation of Gesture in the Works of Chinul (知訥) and Merleau-Ponty
abstract_kr: This thesis is an attempt to better understand language as it is used in kong-an (公案, 공안) practice with particular emphasis on hwadu (話頭, 화두). These logically opaque and often contradictory, poem-like stanzas can appear to lack basic structure. However, the practice of hwadu is a well-established and sophisticated practice used commonly in Buddhism, particularly in the Seon (禪, 선) tradition. The aim of this essay is to give a brief account of hwadu practice as taught by Chinul (知訥, 지눌) and show how logically inconsistent language can be a highly developed means of communicating, especially concerning orders of truths that lie beyond conventional linguistics.Investigating hwadu practice through the lens of continental philosophy, this essay begins with the work of Park who accounts for the ontological foundations of Chinul as well as Merleau- Ponty, especially as they apply to language. Following this is an explanation of Saussure and the influence he had on Merleau- Ponty. In particular, “langue” and “parole”, their significance in explaining what Merleau-Ponty means by “gesture” and what that means for the disclosure of truth will be considered. Furthermore, these considerations will be applied to hwadu practice and suggestions made regarding how they are helpful to understanding the role that language plays therein.

title_kr: 신라 불사리장엄의 전통에 대하여 ― 주요 유물과 연구 쟁점을 중심으로
title_en: On the Tradition of Buddhist Relic Veneration during the Silla: Major Artifacts and Issues
abstract_kr: The kingdom of Silla accepted the Buddhist relic cult for the first time from the middle part of the sixth century through exchanges with Liang dynasty (502-557) of China. Veneration of relics was one of the effective means for Silla rulers, who officially adopted Buddhism, to pose as a wheel-turning king. The construction of a monumental Buddhist pagoda applying the most advanced technology was a way of visually clarifying the power of the ruler as skill and cost were a necessity for building anything of grandeur and prestige. Containers of various types, often made of precious materials and decorated splendidly, functioned to frame those enshrined inside such pagodas as the sacred remains and, by extension, the presence of the Buddha. This article reviews the formation and changes in the reliquary practice developed during the Silla period while paying special attention to the peculiarities of reliquary as an art medium. It concentrates on the mid-Silla (654-780) since many examples from the period have come to light through archaeological excavations and they have received focused scholarly attention for their artistic and religious significance. By doing so, it aims to introduce recent archaeological and art historical research on Buddhist pagodas and relic deposits from the mid-Silla period to a wider community of scholars.

title_kr: 한국 근대 불교문화 사진의 아카이브 구축과 향후과제 - 사진자료의 범위와 가치를 중심으로
title_en: Assignment and Establishing Archives of Modern Korean Buddhist Culture Photos
abstract_kr: This paper looked back on the temporal range and value of the photographic materials used in the ‘Establishing Archives of Modern Korean Buddhist Culture Photos’, and looked at how the constructed photos can be used in the future.First of all, in the study of Korean modern Buddhist cultural photo archives, the reason why the modern time range was assumed to be the 1980s, which is 100 years after 1880 was explained.By taking an example of the fact that photographs related to Buddhist paintings or sculptures belong to the category of photographs showing Buddhist culture, not just works, I explained what the value of photographs is and how it can be used.It is expected that the study of modern Buddhist culture will be expanded by understanding Korean modern culture easily and incorporating it with new fields by being utilized in various fields not only for educational purposes but also in various fields through the ‘Establishing Archives of Modern Korean Buddhist Culture Photos’.

title_kr: 함께 읽기의 즐거움 Thesuarus Literaturae Buddhicae의 현재와 발전방향
title_en: Thesaurus Literaturae Buddhicae: Its Present, and Plans for the Future
abstract_kr: Thesaurus Literaturae Buddhicae (TLB) is a digital archive project of Buddhist literature initiated by Jens Braarvig in 2000 in order to document historically and culturally significant Buddhist texts which have been translated into various languages over the past two millennia. In this paper, as a follow-up study of “Thesaurus Literaturae Buddhicae (TLB): Its Scope, and a Description of Its Routines” (Braarvig: 2001), we examine the present state of TLB, including its achievements and challenges over the past 20 years. We also discuss plans for its further development as a tool for research and education in the field of Buddhist studies. It is hoped that this paper will make a small contribution to promoting the use of this online multilingual digital library, drawing the attention of students, scholars, and the general public in Korea.

title_kr: 기술발전에 의한 불전기록 방법 변화
title_en: Change of Buddhist Texts with Digital Technology Advancement
abstract_kr: This paper aims to suggest a compilation method of electronic documents for Buddhist, with the focus laid on Buddhist elements in the records, which is one of the digital methodologies for analyzing and interpreting source materials in humanities research areas.In the digital era, the concept of “digital encyves” a convergence of digital encyclopedia and digital archives and its development has a significant meaning. In Korea, the Electronic Buddhist Text & Cultural contents partly covers the role of digital archives in terms of the Buddhist elements from Buddhist historical records.Buddhist texts were memorized and handed over by a group of specialists in order to reduce errors occurred due to the individual differences in memory and to keep the original messages of the Buddha intact within the original Buddhist sangha. Electronic Buddhist texts have so far developed and digitized individually by leading institutes scattered around the world. Through cross link between databases, each electronic Buddhist text could be provided by end-users and Buddhist specialists. This could provide solution to correct errors contained in each electronic Buddhist text and to encourage specialists in the area of Buddhist studies to work together. This International Collaboration could show one of the ways to link various Buddhist texts, dictionaries and culture content operating together.Fore the future, we can expect that the revolution in scholarship brought about by the availability of primary source materials in digital format will continue as people find new ways to take advantage of the efficiencies of preservation, access, and searchability engendered by digitalization.

title_kr: 불교사전들이 나아가야 할 길로서 ‘개방자원’
title_en: Open Resources as a Path for Buddhist Dictionaries and Cyclopedias
abstract_kr: We looked at some examples of Buddhist dictionaries and how modern dictionaries are being used by Wiki. As a result, I can conclude that the path to the Buddhist dictionary should be open to a wide range of open resources, and the ‘dictionary’ and the ‘cyclopedia’ should be integrated. In addition, rather than constantly reproducing a dictionary definition, it is a method of quoting the definition being made by the authors of each field in the paper and presenting the paper as a reference. Pre-producers do not have to pay additional costs for writings, and at the same time the authors of the paper get the results of already completed papers being quoted and exposed further. All these values are possible because they are based on a web platform that provides easy access to the web. If Indian traditions pursued certain ultimate things, such as “the ultimate thing (siddhanta)”, “the supreme truth(paramartha)”, and “without superior (anuttara)”, of course the same is true, but when Buddhism was read in the context of China, it was rather “all equipped (具足)” and completely (圓滿). These concepts are safe regardless of context, so they are suitable for any theoretical formula or tool, and we may be too familiar with them. The problem, however, is that in academic descriptions these traditions are so vague that it is impossible to know exactly what each individual seeks.

title_kr: 심우장의 어제와 오늘 - 한용운과 심우장의 정신사 -
title_en: Shim Woo Jang's Yesterday and Today - The Psychological History of Han Yong Woon and Shim Woo Jang -
abstract_kr: This papers is a historical review of Shim Woo jang(심우장), a residence where Han, Yong Woon(한용운) stayed for 10 years before he entered the come to death(1944.6.29). In Han, Yong woon's research so far, Shim Woo jang has not received much attention. However, Shim Woo jang has recently been designated as a national historic site. Recognizing the need for cardiac research, the author wanted to summarize it.In this article, the contents of Shim Woo jang were explained in several ways. First, we looked at Han, Yong Woon's activities before moving into Shimwujiang based on the evidence. He stayed at Seonhakwon(선학원) for 10 years after the March 1st Movement in 1919. Then in the early 1930s, he left Seonhakwon and stayed at a private house in Cheongjin-dong and Sajik-dong, downtown Seoul. Second, Han, Yong woon married in 1933 and wrote about his life in Seongbuk-dong. Third, Han, Yong Woon explained that he had created his own space by using the land and resources provided by his colleague, which was a serious problem. Although the date of its establishment was previously referred to as 1933, I proved that it was 1935. Fourth, the character and identity of Shim Woo jang in which Han, Yong Woon was active. Han, Yong Woon's activities, history in Shim Woo jang, and various writings from his days as Shim Woo-jang were organized. Fifth, the details of Shim's succession were compiled. After Han, Yong Woon's entry into the army, he looked at the protection of the late Manhae descendant Shim Woo jang, the succession project of Han, Yong Woon in Shim Woo jang, and the preservation efforts of Shim Woo jang.We hope the article will help us understand Shim's re-recognition, Han, Yong Woon's perception of the latter half of life, and the preservation activities of the Korean independence fighters' sites.

title_kr: 조계사의 창건과정과 종단 건설
title_en: The Construction Process of Jogyesa and the Establishment of Buddhist Orders
abstract_kr: Jogyesa(曹溪寺) is the headquarters of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism(대한불교조계종). The construction of Jogyesa’s Daewoongjeon Hall(大雄殿) was in 1937 when the construction movement of Korean Buddhist’s headquarters(總本山建設運動) is in progress during the Japanese colonial period. The Daewoongjeon Hall was completed in 1938, and the Korean Buddhist’s headquarters was approved by the Governor-General under the name Taegosa(太古寺). Soon after, the Joseon Buddhist Jogye Order(朝鮮佛敎曹溪宗) was approved by the Governor-General in 1940 and the Taegosa’s law(太古寺法) in 1941. This means that the Joseon Buddhist Jogye Order was recognized as a modern religious organization and officially began its activities. After liberation from Japanese colonial rule, Korean Buddhism tried to eliminate Japanese-style Buddhism, and in the process, the Sangha was divided into single Buddhist monks(比丘僧) and married Buddhist priests(帶妻僧). At that time, the single Buddhist monks changed Taegosa to the name of Jogyesa. Those who had been fighting seriously around Jogyesa, eventually reconciled and created Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism in 1962.Taegosa is the result of the headquarters construction movement during the Japanese colonial period, and Daewoongjeon Hall is the symbolic building of the headquarters and is also the central place in Jogyesa. The construction of the Daeungjeon Hall in Jogyesa became the foundation for the development of the Korean Buddhist Order. Jogyesa was a place where monks gathered to share opinions, and it was a place to solve various problems of the Jogye Order. Therefore, I think that Jogyesa’s status in Korean Buddhism is very high.
keywords_en: the construction movement of Korean Buddhist’s headquarters

title_kr: 대한불교천태종 총본산 구인사 창건과 그 의미
title_en: The meaning of Korean Buddhist Temple Guinsa, the Headquarters of the Cheontae Order, in Korean Buddhism
abstract_kr: Korean Buddhist Temple Guinsa has been the headquarter of the Cheontae Order of Korean Buddhism and has played a central role in Korean Avalokitesvara Cult. The Cheontae Order was commemorated during the modern Buddhism by the Sangwol and it is now one of the representative Buddhist temples in Korea and a sacred place of the Avalokitesvara Cult. In this paper, unlike the previous studies on the geopolitics of Buddhist temple or the study of Buddhist temple placement, this study focuses on the reviewing of the position of Guinsa as a religious sacred place and the shooting as an execution space that has a mass of Buddhist practice.Through this paper, I examined the history of the construction of Guinsa as the headquarter of the Cheontae Order of Korean Buddhism and it can be used to confirm that Guinsa has an important place of worship for the Avalokitesvara Cult in Korea. Unlike the existing Korean temple building culture, Guinsa built temples based on the functionality and practicality of concrete multi-story hanok buildings. However, the inner structure of the central embossed material embodies the mystery of < The Saddharma-pundari-ka-sutra > in the central Buddhiat hall and expressing the Cheontae Order’s identity and discovering the strong embodied the Avalokitesvara Cult.The temple architecture was constructed based on the Buddhist doctrinal system, which means more than just physical reality. As the headquarter of the Cheontae Order of Korean Buddhism, the arrangement of Guinsa is not only providing a space for Buddha and Bodhisattva, but also a place of practice and a place of all sentient being containing the functions and meanings of the ideal world and expression. Korean Buddhist Temple Guinsa is also the center of modern Korean Avalokitesvara Cult along with the Cheontae Order’s performance system as the Buddhist practice in Korea.
keywords_en: The Cheontae Order of Korean Buddhism
The sacred place of the Avalokitesvara Cult

title_kr: 동본원사 부산별원, 그리고 대각사 - 100년을 통해서 본 한국과 일본불교의 ‘공간’의 역사 -
title_en: Busan Branch Temple of Dongbonwonsa Temple and Daegaksa Temple - The History surrounding the ‘Space’ of South Korean and Japanese Buddhism viewed through 100 Years -
abstract_kr: Busan Daegaksa Temple is a temple of the Jogye Order (Address: 1-ga Sinchang-dong Jung-gu, Busan), which is located in the center of the fashion street of Gwangbok-dong, downtown Busan, unlike other temples. It was formerly ‘Busan Branch Temple of Dongbonwonsa Temple, belonging to Bonwonsa Temple of Jinjongdaegokpa of Japanese Buddhism founded on November 5, 1877. It is the temple founded first by the Japanese people, which has a significant meaning, marking a milestone in the modern history of Korea. This study would discuss the historical meaning of the ‘space’ of South Korean and Japanese Buddhism appearing in the history of 100 years, starting from Busan Branch Temple of Dongbonwonsa Temple in 1877 to Daegaksa Temple in 1976. For this purpose, this study would investigate the status of the propagation activities and various projects of Busan Branch Temple of Dongbonwonsa Temple starting 1877 and the dispute over the ownership surrounding the Daegaksa Temple space in the South Korean Buddhist Community after the restoration of independence until 1976.
keywords_en: Busan Branch Temple of Dongbonwonsa Temple

Academic theorem, research, and reflection on oral history in the Buddhist world are insignificant. Therefore, we considered the nature of data to be active in this field research. Third, I emphasized the importance of oral interview work in the study of the high priest.I hope that this review will be a reference to the Buddhist oral history, the study of the high priest, and the extension of the modern and modern Buddhist sphere.

title_kr: 호암당 채인환 회고록의 구술사적 가치
title_en: Filming of Hoam Chainhwan(1931-2018)'s Oral Memoir and Its Value
abstract_kr: Hoamdang Inhwan is a Great Master of Jogye Order Who equipped with Seon, Doctrine, and Vinya, and is a professor and dharma-bhanaka. He was born in Wonsan and settled in Busan when he retired 1.4 retreat and was became a monk in Seonamsa Temple. Chae In-hwan met the distinguished teachers gathered at the temple, who were from the Mahayana seon center at Mt. Kumgang. He had a good chance of receiving their lessons. Later, he completed his degrees in Korea and Japan, passed through Canada and worked as a professor at Dongguk University. His major was Sila-Vinaya, who preached before his Parinirvana. He passed away on October 26, 2018 after putting his life into a phraseology. Chae's oral version, which started in 2011, ended in his memoirs in 2017. His gifts of oral materials were left to the nation's history and the Jogye Order as a subject of future generations.While I was preparing a paper for Chae In-hwan's essay, he died, and I donated it. He is a stern teacher, but he lived in this world with integrity and purity. Chae has long planned to keep his experience on record, and I took charge of it. I applied digital technology to this memoir. I made his video, collected and photographed, and edited the film to make it on CD.Chaeinhwan the horrors of war, and the Pacific during the Japanese occupation as turmoil after liberation. And he experienced the horrors of the Korean War. However, he entered the temple and became a Buddhist monk, which stood in a completely different place. He had a special bond with two monks here. He trained himself harshly and left the stories behind in his memoirs. As a scholar, he sought to objectify, document and also make meaning for his memories. It is rather easy to read and understand the history of the times. In this regard, his memoirs can be used as references to produce other works.

title_kr: 천태종단사와 구술사
title_en: History of Cheontae Order and its Oral History
abstract_kr: In this paper, I examined the history of the Cheontae religious order and the Oral history of the Cheontae Order of Korean Buddhism through the Interview Work by the central organization of its order. Also, I reviewed the life history of the founder of the Cheontae Order of Korean Buddhism, focusing on the monographs published in Buddhist academy inside and outside. Through this, a proposal for oral work was derived for the current Buddhist system. First, it is essential to educate researchers who are engaged in oral history. Second, preliminary investigation of the Buddhist personality which is the center of dictation, question and discussion about it should be preceded. Third, the collection of photographs or documents related to the dictated matters should be done together with the oral work. Fourth, after the oral work, the interviewee should confirm the contents and document the notarization or consent for utilization of the data. Fifth, the contents recorded after the oral work should be accessible to the general public. Sixth, Korean Modern Buddhist Venerable Oral Archives should be constructed.

Korean Modern Buddhist Venerable Oral Archives

title_kr: 불교 구술 아카이브 구축과 활용
title_en: The Construction and Utilization of an Buddhist Oral Archives
abstract_kr: This study had contemplation over the ways of organizing and utilizing oral statement outcomes for the utilization of Buddhist history and culture. Today the oral history of Buddhism is making achievements in academic research including the organization of new historical materials and the establishment of a foundation for research on high priests in the modern and contemporary history of Buddhism with a focus on the oral statement achievements regarding high priests.The investigator had contemplation over a direction for the construction and utilization of oral statements as an archive from the perspectives of their collective creativity and two-way communication, focusing on the process of oral statements as the sharing and expansion of memories.Old archives had primary goals of collection, preservation, and approach by users. The study examined the current state of public archives of oral statements and discussed the possibilities of and need for an archive of oral statements about Buddhism. A focus was placed on the characteristics of oral statements including the inheritance of culture and sharing of memories as a way of sorting out oral statement materials about Buddhism right and putting them to various uses. In addition, the study discussed the prospects of utilization in the space of Buddhist temples in the field of spatial storytelling with a focus on the placeness of oral statement memories.The study will hopefully contribute to further discussions about the need for an archive of oral statements about Buddhism.

title_kr: <부록>화과원의 역사, 문화의 구술 증언
백용성의 『금강경』에 대한 이해
title_en: Baek Yong-seong’s Understanding of Vajracchedika Prajnaparamita-sutra
abstract_kr: Back Yong-seong wrote three books on Vajracchedika Prajnaparamita-sutra. It seems that he dedicated himself to studying Vajracchedika Prajnaparamita-sutra from the age of 57 to 60. He left three different books on Vajracchedika Prajnaparamita-sutra and they have the following features.First, in Sinyuk Daejanggyung Gumganggyung-Ganguil (『新譯大藏 經金剛經講義』), the author exposited 112 sections after dividing the Sutra into 113 sections on the basis of the existing 32 parts. Second, Sinyuk Daejang Gumgang Maha-Prajnaparamita-sutra (『新譯大藏金剛摩 訶般若波羅蜜經』) added the author’s thoughts focused on Yefu-Daochuan (冶父道川, 1127-1130)’s theory among Hamhu-Duktong’s Gumgang Maha-Prajnaparamita-sutra Oga Haeseoleui (『金剛般若波羅蜜經五家解說誼』). Third, in Sangyuk Gwahae Gumgang-gyung (『詳譯科解金剛經』), Yong-seong newly explained Vajracchedika Prajnaparamita-sutra not being influenced by both the existing 32 parts and Oga Haeseoleui. In comparing these three kinds of Vajracchedika Prajnaparamita-sutra books, we can verify that Yong-seong’s understanding of Vajracchedika Prajnaparamita-sutra grew gradually deepened.The fact that Yong-seong wrote three different books on Vajracchedika Prajnaparamita-sutra means his level of understanding of the Sutra developed. When we discuss a person’s thought, it is commonly accepted to judge through his last book or article. Because the person’s thought becomes more elaborated and elevated with the passage of time. In this respect, it is needless to say that Yong-seong’s understanding of Vajracchedika Prajnaparamita-sutra should be based on his third book Sangyuk Gwahae Gumgang-gyung.

title_kr: 율풍진작(律風振作)을 통(通)한 한국불교 중흥(中興)의 행적(行蹟)
title_en: Process of Korean Buddhism’s Restoration through Boosting the Precepts Promotion
abstract_kr: This paper is to arrange the traces of the priest Jaun (1911~1992), who was the central figure for boosting Korean Buddhism in modern times, and especially, the contents called the process of Korean Buddhism’s restoration through boosting the precepts promotion. I once released a paper under the title of ‘The priest Jaun’s long journey for Harmonized Buddhism and Scripture Translation.’However, Gasan Pilgrims’ Association and Gasan Buddhist Culture Research Center offered academic events on the priest Jaun such as the 1st symposium on the priest Jaun’s precepts enhancement (Gyeongguksa Temple, 2005), the 2nd symposium commemorating the 100th year of his birth (International conference room of Jogye order, 2013), and a seminar commemorating the launch of Jaun’s Commandments Research Center. However, there still are much to research on the priest Jaun.Under this circumstance, I will prove that the priest Jaun’s precepts promotion was the foundation for developing Korean Buddhism, especially for the Jogye Order. The detailed contents are composed of his research on precepts, publishment of Vinaya Pitaka, foundation of the religious order Danilgyedan, establishment of the system called Ibuseungje Sugye, opening of Sugyesallim and lectures on precepts, and contents of education for people.I hope that this paper could be a help for researching on the priest Jaun, history of Jogye Order’s precepts style, publishment of Vinaya Pitaka, Danilgyedan, Sugyesallim, Yulwon and Yulsa.

title_kr: 백초월 독립운동의 성격 - 용성·만해와 비교하여 본 단면 -
title_en: Characteristics of Baek Cho-wol’s Independence Movement - Comparing to that of Yongseong and Manhae -
abstract_kr: This paper is to find out the characteristics and position of the national movement of Baek Cho-wol (1878∼1944) who was recently recognized as one of the fighters for independence. To do this, I tried to analyze by comparing him with Baek Yong-seong and Manhae Han Yong-un who were the Buddhist fighter for independence of the modern times. This idea came from my belief that we have to understand Baek Cho-wol, Baek Yong-seong and Han Yong-un equally.Based on this background, I have compared Chowol with Yongseong and Manhae. Therefore, as the viewpoint of the research on Baek Cho-wol, I propose the identity called Gangbaek, Gangwon, the fact that he directed the domestic Buddhists’ independence movement, his relationships with the provisional government and the national independence army in Manchuria, and a detailed approach to Ilsimgyo.With regard to the representative 3 figures (Yongseong, Manhae and Chowol) of Buddhist fighters for independence that I have emphasized, I would propose a reconsideration for the recognition of them. abstract_kr: This study investigates the Buddhist Sangha reformation movement of Yongseong and its development with a consideration of circumstances during his lifetime. The life of Yongseong was solely given to the implementation of Supreme Enlightenment. In order to realize this goal, he asserted all Buddhists should practice three guidelines for edification. These are making Buddhism as everyday life, popularization of Buddhism and intellectualization of Buddhism. Here the last guideline is mainly focused in terms of Yongseong`s reformation. The period when Yongseong lived was from the Joseon Dynasty, which was changed into the Korean Empire later, to the Japanese colonial rule. He lived through a gloomy era for the whole Korean nation. Besides, the period was going through great changes in almost every sector including politics, economy, society and culture. In the history of Korean Buddhism, this period is called `modern Buddhism` and Yongseong lived in this period of upheaval. In the era of modern Korean Buddhism, crisis and opportunity coexisted. Modern Korean Buddhism had an opportunity of new development by overcoming the Joseon Kingdom`s policy of Buddhism suppression. At the same time, it faced a crisis as the Japanese Buddhism landed on the Korean Peninsula and Christianity expanded. By using the chance, Buddhist monks of this period tried to revive Joseon Buddhism which had suffered a serious decline. The existing Buddhism, they thought, failed to adapt to the rapidly changing age. In this context, a modern Buddhism reformation movement emerged. The reformation movement revealed two characteristics in those years. One is a reflection on the traditional aspect of the Buddhist Sangha and the other is a strong practical belief to pursue a new form of existence. The former began with the recognition of the Joseon Buddhist community that should be changed. And the latter was based on the idea of the then incompetent Buddhist Sangha which must adopt new Western civilization to develop itself abreast of the times. But the reformation ideas from the Buddhist leaders of the period were not intended to return to the pure Sangha, but rather to accelerate its secularization. On the contrary, the Sangha reformation movement of Yongseong concentrated on new edification activities by keeping the traditions of Joseon Buddhism through a purification of the Buddhist community, not by means of its secularization and blocking out any foreign influences. In other words, Yongseong meditated in anguish how to regain the sovereignty of Korea and to restore the identity ofwas the idea of `Supreme Enlightenment.` With this idea, Yongseong made every effort to establish the identity of Joseon Buddhism and to develop edifying campaigns proper to the period. For this purpose, reformation was a must. Yongseong`s reformation campaigns were implemented in diverse ways. title_kr: 용성선사의 죽음관 연구 - 『림종결(臨終訣)』을 중심으로 -
title_en: A Study for Yongseong`s Thoughts of Death - Focusing on Im-J ong-Gyeol (臨終訣) -
abstract_kr: In this article, I explored Zen master Yongseong`s view of death through the Im-jong-gyeol(臨終訣) which was written by books Yongseong. Im-jong-gyeol is the book for attitudes and practices on dying and that is composed of interlocutory. Although the subject of Im-jonggyeol is death, terms like Daegak(大覺), Jeongto(淨土), alaya-vijnana (第八識) often are seen in that book. From that point, there are many things, like the thoughts of Dasheng qixin lun(大乘起信論), Yogacara, Jeongto(淨土) etc. in Im-jong-gyeol. Therefore, Im-jong-gyeol is not death related book but comprehensive book which contains Yongseong`s essential thoughts. Im-jong-gyeol is constructed by eight subjects; ① `bonche(本體)of bonseong(本性)`, ② `life and death on acting of bonche(本體)`, ③ `prepar-ing of death on living`, ④ `way to overcome on dying`, ⑤ `way to rebirth in Pure Land(淨土)`, ⑥ `way to samadhi`, ⑦ `mention for spirit` etc. Zen master Yongseong emphasizes practice for peaceful death on living and suggests yeombul(念佛), chamseon(參禪), gangyeong(看經), juryeok(呪力) in his books. Ultimately, Im-jong-gyeol is the representa-tive Yongseong`s book which is for death and dying and he suggests way to preparing for death.

abstract_kr: Numerous high priests of Buddhism such as Gyeongheo, Mangong, Yongseong, Seokjeon, Pangong, Hanam, Manhae, Seongcul and Unheo have appeared upon the sphere of Korean Buddhism through the times of Japanese colonial rule, Korean war and industrialization of the nation. They encouraged Korean people who were suffered from the tough times by Buddha``s lesson, and were engaged in various social activities. With this Korean Buddhists made an attempt to break out of long-term depression of Buddhism of Korea.  However, there remain few relics of the modern or contemporary high priests of Buddhism in Korea. It makes their lives, philosophies and achievements be hard to be studied in Korea. It is because of lack of effort to socialize their lives by means of objective academic studies, which is derived from lack of information and data as mentioned frequently. The paper explores to learn the possibility to find a new method to study on the issue mentioned so as to overcome the realistic problems, and revealed the results of actual analysis. And it suggests analysis of desk diary as a new research method. Monks of Buddhism were usually highbrow class in the era of later Joseon, Japanese colonial rule and liberation of Nation. They had a tendency to put down their thoughts and activities, and a diary was a dominant form for writing in those days. Though the diaries were forgotten for a while during the tough time due to the weakened interest, a new light started to shed on their records concerned as the interest from Buddhism increased recently.  Nevertheless, the fact that researchers are not familiar with such an analysis method of diary and uncertain about research value of analysis of diary makes researchers reluctant to study on high priests I lives, philosophies and activities. In this paper, method of analysis of diaries is arranged and an example of objective analysis and interpretation of the arrangement is shown. abstract_kr: This study aims to analyze life and thoughts of venerable Wonhyo who lived in Silla Dynasty in 7th century, and to investigate the contemporary impact of his two signature ideas: the unconstrained conduct, the reconciliation theory. These ideas still have a great significance. Venerable Wonhyo was a thinker with a practical mind. His thoughts and study were not bound for metaphysical subjects but aimed at a substantial practice. His thoughts were expressed in his Buddhist studies and he practiced those thoughts on the practical level through the edification of the people. More than a hundred books of his were the fruit of his Buddhist study and he enlightened countless people. A story said that he was an unconstrained existence so that he could show up in hundreds places at a time. Thus he was said that he had entered the stage of great freedom and a saint. Venerable Wonhyo was bound to neither priesthood nor secular life. He lived as a priest and a layman. He recognized that there were contradictions between the secular truth and the sacred truth and he, to solve this problem, emphasized that both secular and sacred truths were harmonious and they were not constrained to anything. His ideas still have a great meaning on the understanding of the world He did not only emphasize Mahayana life but also held Hinayana in great account. The need of normal people for happiness was also very important for him. For him, both rationality and humanity were important. He believed that if these two virtues are inconflict with each other, the solution must satisfy both of them. Reconciliation, for venerable Wonhyo, was the truth of the world and life as well as the methodology of his study and the goal of his practice. His reconciliation theory is about harmonizing two different objects but still preserving their own peculiarities. There are lots of gates; there are lots of ways to reach the gates. There are many principles in the world, but they are not always different from each other. Venerable Wonhyo said ``every gates belongs to every gates because they are not the one; every gates are not different from each other so that every gates tastes the same`` Recognition of diversity is a premise of the reconciliation theory. A conflict is caused by the words we use. If we could see an implication the words have, there would not be any intolerable things. The finger can point to the moon. However, the finger is not the moon. To look at the moon, you must gaze beyond the finger.
